part.text:
All tests pass. I implemented the solution in `dominoes.go`:

- **`Domino`** — defined as `[2]int`, matching how the tests construct and compare stones.
- **`MakeChain`** — a backtracking search: it places each unused domino (tracked by index, so duplicate stones are handled correctly) into the chain in either orientation, requiring the new stone's left half to match the previous stone's right half. When all stones are placed, it checks that the chain closes (`chain[0][0] == chain[last][1]`).

The backtracking handles the tricky cases: it explores both orientations and undoes choices on failure, so it finds chains that require backtracking (like the "need backtrack" case) and correctly rejects disconnected sets that pass the naive even-degree check. Empty input returns an empty chain with `true`, and the singleton `{1,1}` is returned unchanged so it satisfies the test's exact-match check.

`go test ./...` passes all 12 test cases, and no other files were created or modified.
